note: v3 with its rules as a teacher for distillation (agrees with 100.0% of 6000 logged decisions); the teacher's own games: 1485, 1485, 1485.
instructions:
Apply these rules in order and pick the first that matches.
1. If over is true: choose JUMP (restarts the game).
2. If player.air is true: choose NOOP. Never hold JUMP in the air (the key must be released so the next jump is a fresh press).
3. If threat is null: choose NOOP.
4. If threat.duckable is true and threat.impactMs <= 250: choose DUCK (keep choosing DUCK while this holds, until the bird has passed).
5. If threat.jumpTiming is "ok" or "late": choose JUMP.
6. Otherwise (threat.jumpTiming is "early"): choose NOOP and wait.
Notes: threat is the nearest obstacle that can hit the dino (birds flying above the dino and sky decorations such as stars and the moon are already excluded). jumpTiming "early" means a jump started now would come down on the obstacle; "ok" means a jump now clears it; "late" means the best moment has passed, so jump immediately anyway.

actions.description: Jump (only works from the ground with a fresh press), or restart the game
Duck under birds (hold while the bird passes)

tests.why: Night-mode stars (9x9 sprites high in the sky) must never show up as obstacles.
A sky decoration must never become the threat that triggers a jump.
The star that caused the mistimed jump before the small cactus must be filtered out.
With only a star and an overhead bird ahead, the dino must stay on the ground instead of jumping into the bird.
When the dino lands before the large cactus, the threat must be the cactus rather than a star, so the jump is timed to the cactus.
